quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional hospital network's quality committee reviewed outcomes after introducing a new sepsis screening protocol in its emergency departments. Across six hospitals, average time-to-treatment for confirmed sepsis cases dropped from 94 minutes to 61 minutes in the year following implementation. However, the committee noted that the protocol rollout coincided with a broader statewide initiative providing additional emergency department staffing grants, which three of the six hospitals received and three did not. Among the three hospitals that received the staffing grants, time-to-treatment dropped to 48 minutes on average. Among the three that did not receive grants but still implemented the new protocol, time-to-treatment dropped to 74 minutes.
options: The staffing grants alone explain the entire improvement, with the protocol having no measurable effect. Nothing in the passage suggests this changed at any point during the period described.
Hospitals without staffing grants saw no improvement in treatment times at all.

The protocol was only implemented at hospitals that also received staffing grants. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.
Both the new protocol and the additional staffing appear to have contributed to faster treatment times, with staffing showing a notably larger individual effect.
quests.correctAnswer: Both the new protocol and the additional staffing appear to have contributed to faster treatment times, with staffing showing a notably larger individual effect.
quests.hint: Notice that all six hospitals implemented the protocol, but only half received grants, then compare the improvement sizes across both subgroups.
quests.explanation: Since all six hospitals adopted the protocol but showed different improvement levels based on grant status, both factors appear to matter: the protocol alone improved things at non-grant hospitals (94 to 74 minutes), while the addition of staffing produced a larger combined effect (94 to 48 minutes) at grant hospitals.
logicChain: All 6 hospitals implement new protocol -> 3 also receive staffing grants, 3 don't -> non-grant hospitals: 94 to 74 min -> grant hospitals: 94 to 48 min -> protocol shows an effect alone, staffing appears to add a further, larger effect

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national retailer's loyalty program overhaul replaced a simple points-per-dollar system with a tiered structure offering escalating perks at spending thresholds. In the six months following the change, top-tier members, representing about 8 percent of the loyalty base, increased their spending by 34 percent. Mid-tier members, about 35 percent of the base, increased spending by 11 percent. The remaining 57 percent of members, who fell below the lowest tier threshold and received no immediate perks under the new structure, decreased their spending by 4 percent compared to the previous year.
options: The new tiered structure appears to have rewarded and further engaged higher-spending members while potentially discouraging members who didn't reach a rewarded tier.
All members, regardless of tier, increased their spending by roughly the same amount.
The new structure caused spending to decrease across every member segment.
Members below the lowest tier threshold saw the largest spending increase.
quests.correctAnswer: The new tiered structure appears to have rewarded and further engaged higher-spending members while potentially discouraging members who didn't reach a rewarded tier.
quests.hint: Compare the spending change across all three described groups, noting both the direction and size of each change.
quests.explanation: The data shows a clear gradient: spending increases were largest among top-tier members and smaller among mid-tier members, while members who received no new perks actually decreased spending, suggesting the tiered structure both rewarded higher spenders and may have discouraged those left without new incentives.
logicChain: Top tier (8%): spending +34% -> mid tier (35%): spending +11% -> below threshold (57%), no new perks: spending -4% -> gradient suggests the tiers rewarded higher spenders while potentially discouraging those without new incentives

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's juvenile justice department piloted a restorative justice program as an alternative to traditional court proceedings for certain first-time, non-violent offenses. Participants in the program, who were required to complete a series of mediated conversations with those affected by their actions along with community service, had a one-year re-offense rate of 12 percent. Youth who went through traditional court proceedings for comparable offenses during the same period had a re-offense rate of 27 percent. However, participation in the restorative program required both the youth and their guardian to consent, and roughly 40 percent of eligible youth declined to participate.
options: While the results are promising for participants, the voluntary nature of the program means the comparison may partly reflect differences between families who opted in and those who did not.
The restorative justice program is proven to reduce re-offense rates for any youth who is required to complete it.
Traditional court proceedings had a lower re-offense rate than the restorative justice program.
All eligible youth were required to participate in the restorative justice program.
quests.correctAnswer: While the results are promising for participants, the voluntary nature of the program means the comparison may partly reflect differences between families who opted in and those who did not.
quests.hint: Weigh the promising outcome difference against the detail about voluntary participation and the significant decline rate.
quests.explanation: Since participation was voluntary and a substantial share of eligible youth declined, families who opted in may differ systematically, in motivation, family support, or other factors, from those who didn't, meaning the comparison, while promising, can't be fully separated from this self-selection.
logicChain: Program participants: 12% re-offense -> traditional court: 27% re-offense -> participation requires consent, 40% of eligible youth decline -> voluntary nature means self-selection may partly explain the difference, complicating a fully clean comparison

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An agricultural extension office studied crop yields across 200 farms after roughly half adopted a new soil-moisture sensor system that provided real-time irrigation recommendations. Farms using the sensors saw average yield increases of 14 percent compared to their five-year historical average. Farms not using the sensors saw yield increases of 6 percent over the same period, which the office attributed to an unusually favorable growing season affecting the entire region. Sensor-using farms also reported using 22 percent less water on average than non-sensor farms.
options: The favorable growing season fully explains the yield increase at sensor-using farms, with the sensors themselves having no additional effect. Every relevant detail included in the passage is consistent with treating this as a complete and accurate account, without further qualification being necessary.

Farms without sensors used less water than farms with the sensor system. Reading through everything the passage lays out, there is no specific detail that would push against treating this as the straightforward explanation.

Beyond the region-wide favorable conditions that benefited all farms somewhat, the sensor system appears to have provided an additional yield benefit specifically to the farms that adopted it, while also reducing water use.

Non-sensor farms saw a larger yield increase than sensor-using farms. Nothing in the way the passage lays out these events gives any real reason to treat this as an incomplete or qualified reading of what took place.
quests.correctAnswer: Beyond the region-wide favorable conditions that benefited all farms somewhat, the sensor system appears to have provided an additional yield benefit specifically to the farms that adopted it, while also reducing water use.
quests.hint: Separate the region-wide baseline improvement, seen in non-sensor farms, from the additional gain specific to sensor-using farms.
quests.explanation: Since non-sensor farms already show a 6 percent gain attributable to favorable regional conditions, the sensor farms' additional gain beyond that, 14 percent versus 6 percent, suggests the technology provided a real benefit on top of the broader seasonal advantage, along with a separate, clear reduction in water use.
logicChain: Non-sensor farms: +6% yield, attributed to favorable regional season -> sensor farms: +14% yield -> sensor farms also use 22% less water -> additional gain beyond the regional baseline suggests a real, specific sensor benefit, plus a clear water-use reduction

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large accounting firm compared employee performance reviews before and after introducing a policy allowing employees to choose between traditional annual reviews and a new continuous feedback system with monthly check-ins. Employees who chose continuous feedback showed a 15 percent increase in projects completed on time compared to their own performance the prior year. Employees who kept the traditional annual review system showed no significant change in on-time project completion. Notably, employees who chose continuous feedback were, on average, three years less senior than those who kept the traditional system.
options: The continuous feedback system is proven to be the sole cause of the improvement, independent of any other employee characteristic. Reading through everything the passage lays out, there is no specific detail that would push against treating this as the straightforward explanation.

Employees who kept the traditional review system were less senior than those who switched. The full account given in the passage offers no particular basis for reading this any differently than as a plain, straightforward description of events.

On-time project completion decreased for employees who chose continuous feedback. Nothing in the way the passage lays out these events gives any real reason to treat this as an incomplete or qualified reading of what took place.

Since continuous feedback users were also less senior on average, it is difficult to fully separate the effect of the feedback system from the effect of being earlier in one's career, where performance might naturally be more likely to improve.
quests.correctAnswer: Since continuous feedback users were also less senior on average, it is difficult to fully separate the effect of the feedback system from the effect of being earlier in one's career, where performance might naturally be more likely to improve.
quests.hint: Consider what the seniority difference between the two groups might independently suggest about their likely trajectory of improvement.
quests.explanation: Since continuous feedback users were notably less senior, and less experienced employees might show natural performance gains as they develop regardless of feedback style, this seniority gap complicates confidently attributing the full improvement to the feedback system itself.
logicChain: Continuous feedback users: +15% on-time completion vs. prior year -> traditional review users: no significant change -> feedback users also 3 years less senior on average -> seniority gap complicates fully isolating the feedback system's specific effect

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's housing authority evaluated a supportive housing program that paired formerly homeless individuals with subsidized apartments and on-site case management. Over two years, 71 percent of program participants remained stably housed, compared to a national benchmark of 45 percent for similar populations without case management support. The program also reported that participants' use of emergency room services dropped by 58 percent compared to their own usage in the two years prior to enrollment, and the authority calculated this reduction saved an estimated $1.2 million in emergency healthcare costs, partially offsetting the program's $2.8 million operating budget.
options: The estimated healthcare savings fully covered the program's entire operating budget. Every relevant detail included in the passage is consistent with treating this as a complete and accurate account, without further qualification being necessary.

Participants' emergency room usage increased after enrolling in the program. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.
The program shows strong housing stability results and appears linked to reduced emergency healthcare use, though the cost savings only partially offset the program's total operating expenses.

The program's housing stability rate was lower than the national benchmark for similar populations. Nothing about how the passage frames the surrounding circumstances would suggest this conclusion needs any further qualification or limitation.
quests.correctAnswer: The program shows strong housing stability results and appears linked to reduced emergency healthcare use, though the cost savings only partially offset the program's total operating expenses.
quests.hint: Track three separate figures: the housing stability rate, the healthcare usage change, and how the cost savings compare to the total budget.
quests.explanation: The passage supports three specific, related findings: higher stable housing rates than the benchmark, a substantial drop in participants' own emergency room use, and healthcare savings that are explicitly described as only 'partially offsetting' the larger operating budget, not fully covering it.
logicChain: Housing stability: 71% vs. 45% benchmark -> ER usage drops 58% vs. participants' own prior usage -> estimated savings: $1.2M, described as 'partially offsetting' the $2.8M budget -> strong outcomes with savings that only partially cover total costs

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national parks service conducted a multi-year study on trail erosion at popular hiking destinations. Trails that received a new boardwalk surface in high-traffic sections showed erosion rates 78 percent lower than trails without boardwalks over three years. However, boardwalk installation was prioritized for trails already showing the most severe erosion damage, meaning these trails also received additional volunteer-led erosion control efforts, including replanting native vegetation along trail edges, that were not part of a formal, separately tracked program at non-boardwalk trails.
options: Since boardwalk trails also received extra volunteer erosion control that wasn't tracked separately, it is difficult to isolate how much of the erosion reduction is specifically due to the boardwalks themselves.

The boardwalks are proven to be entirely responsible for the erosion reduction, with no other contributing factors. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.
Trails without boardwalks received more volunteer erosion control efforts than trails with boardwalks.
Erosion rates increased at trails that received the new boardwalk surfaces.
quests.correctAnswer: Since boardwalk trails also received extra volunteer erosion control that wasn't tracked separately, it is difficult to isolate how much of the erosion reduction is specifically due to the boardwalks themselves.
quests.hint: Notice that two changes, boardwalks and untracked volunteer efforts, both occurred together specifically at the most severely eroded trails.
quests.explanation: Because boardwalk trails also received additional volunteer restoration work that wasn't tracked as a separate variable, and both changes happened together specifically at the most severe erosion sites, it's difficult to cleanly attribute the full erosion reduction to the boardwalks alone.
logicChain: Boardwalks prioritized for most severely eroded trails -> those trails also get untracked volunteer erosion control -> boardwalk trails: 78% lower erosion -> two simultaneous, non-separated interventions make it difficult to isolate the boardwalk's specific contribution

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A telecommunications company analyzed customer churn after launching two initiatives in the same quarter: a redesigned mobile app with simplified bill payment, and a new customer retention team empowered to offer personalized discounts to at-risk customers identified by a churn-prediction algorithm. Overall churn dropped from 2.8 percent monthly to 1.9 percent monthly. Among customers who used the redesigned app at least once, churn was 1.2 percent. Among customers flagged by the algorithm and offered a retention discount, churn was 0.8 percent regardless of app usage. Customers who neither used the new app nor were flagged by the algorithm churned at 2.6 percent, close to the original baseline.
options: Only the app redesign had any measurable effect on churn, with the retention discounts showing no impact. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.

Customers who were not reached by either initiative showed the largest reduction in churn. The way the events are described throughout the passage offers no clear signal that this particular reading should be treated with any extra caution.
Overall churn increased after both initiatives were introduced.
Both initiatives appear linked to reduced churn among the customers they specifically reached, while customers untouched by either initiative saw little change from the original rate.
quests.correctAnswer: Both initiatives appear linked to reduced churn among the customers they specifically reached, while customers untouched by either initiative saw little change from the original rate.
quests.hint: Compare churn rates across the three described customer segments, noting which ones were actually reached by an initiative.
quests.explanation: Customers reached by either the app or the retention discounts show meaningfully lower churn than customers untouched by both initiatives, whose rate stayed close to the original baseline, supporting both initiatives as linked to the improvement specifically among the customers they reached.
logicChain: Overall churn: 2.8% to 1.9% -> app users: 1.2% churn -> algorithm-flagged, discount recipients: 0.8% churn -> untouched by either: 2.6%, close to baseline -> both initiatives appear linked to reduced churn among reached customers

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university's admissions office studied the predictive value of an optional applicant interview after several years of data collection. Applicants who scored highly in their interview had a four-year graduation rate of 84 percent. Applicants who scored poorly in their interview had a graduation rate of 71 percent. However, when the office controlled for high school GPA and standardized test scores, factors already strongly predictive of graduation on their own, the remaining difference attributable to interview score alone narrowed to just 3 percentage points, which the office's statisticians noted was within the range that could be explained by normal data variation.
options: The interview score is proven to be the strongest predictor of graduation, independent of academic factors.
Once academic factors already known to predict graduation are accounted for, the interview itself appears to add little additional predictive value on its own.
High school GPA and standardized test scores have no relationship to graduation rates.
The raw graduation rate difference between interview score groups was smaller than the difference after controlling for academic factors, as the passage presents the situation.
quests.correctAnswer: Once academic factors already known to predict graduation are accounted for, the interview itself appears to add little additional predictive value on its own.
quests.hint: Compare the raw, unadjusted difference in graduation rates to the much smaller difference remaining after controlling for other known predictive factors.
quests.explanation: While the raw difference in graduation rates looks meaningful (84 versus 71 percent), controlling for GPA and test scores, both already strong predictors, shrinks the interview-specific difference to just 3 points, a gap the office's own statisticians say could reflect normal variation rather than a real effect of the interview itself.
logicChain: Raw graduation rates: high interview score 84%, low score 71% -> after controlling for GPA and test scores (already strong predictors) -> remaining interview-attributable difference: 3 points, within normal variation -> interview appears to add little independent predictive value once academic factors are accounted for

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A metropolitan police department implemented body cameras department-wide and tracked both citizen complaints and officer use-of-force incidents over the following two years. Complaints against officers dropped 39 percent, and use-of-force incidents dropped 31 percent compared to the two years prior to implementation. A separate analysis found that officers who reviewed their own body camera footage with a supervisor at least monthly showed a 52 percent reduction in use-of-force incidents, while officers who wore cameras but rarely reviewed footage with a supervisor showed only a 9 percent reduction, close to a citywide trend of declining use-of-force incidents that had already begun the year before cameras were introduced, attributed to a separate de-escalation training program.
options: Wearing a body camera alone, regardless of footage review, fully explains the entire reduction in use-of-force incidents. As far as the passage's description goes, nothing about the surrounding details would suggest this needs to be treated as an incomplete picture.

Simply wearing a camera appears to have had a much smaller effect than actively reviewing footage with a supervisor, and even the smaller effect may partly reflect a pre-existing trend from separate training.

Officers who rarely reviewed footage showed a larger reduction than officers who reviewed footage monthly. There is nothing in how the passage presents the sequence of events that would call for treating this conclusion as only partly supported.

The citywide decline in use-of-force incidents began only after body cameras were introduced. Every relevant detail included in the passage is consistent with treating this as a complete and accurate account, without further qualification being necessary.
quests.correctAnswer: Simply wearing a camera appears to have had a much smaller effect than actively reviewing footage with a supervisor, and even the smaller effect may partly reflect a pre-existing trend from separate training.
quests.hint: Compare the two officer subgroups' reduction rates, and note the detail about when the citywide trend actually began relative to camera introduction.
quests.explanation: The stark difference between officers who reviewed footage regularly (52 percent reduction) and those who didn't (9 percent, close to a trend that predates the cameras and is attributed to separate training) suggests the active review process, not merely wearing a camera, drove most of the meaningful improvement.
logicChain: Overall use-of-force: -31% -> regular footage review: -52% -> rare footage review: -9%, close to a citywide trend that began before cameras, attributed to separate de-escalation training -> active review appears to drive most of the effect; passive camera-wearing alone shows little effect beyond a pre-existing trend

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A pharmaceutical benefit manager analyzed the effect of a new prior-authorization requirement for a class of expensive brand-name medications, intended to encourage use of equally effective generic alternatives. In the year following implementation, use of the brand-name medications dropped 61 percent, and overall prescription drug spending for this category fell 24 percent. However, calls to a nurse advice line regarding medication access problems rose 340 percent for this drug category, and a patient advocacy group reported that pharmacies noted increased instances of patients leaving without any medication after their brand-name prescription was rejected and no immediate generic substitution was offered by the prescribing physician.
options: While the policy achieved its cost-reduction goal, the sharp rise in access-related complaints suggests the transition created significant friction for at least some patients.
The policy achieved its cost-reduction goal with no negative effects on patient access reported anywhere. The passage gives no indication that this varied across the circumstances described.

Prescription drug spending in this category increased after the policy was implemented. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.

Calls to the nurse advice line about medication access decreased after the policy began. Every relevant detail included in the passage is consistent with treating this as a complete and accurate account, without further qualification being necessary.
quests.correctAnswer: While the policy achieved its cost-reduction goal, the sharp rise in access-related complaints suggests the transition created significant friction for at least some patients.
quests.hint: Weigh the clear cost and utilization success against the specific, separately reported access complaints and pharmacy observations.
quests.explanation: The passage supports a genuinely mixed picture: the policy clearly succeeded at its stated financial goal, but the dramatic rise in nurse advice line calls and pharmacy reports of patients leaving without medication indicate the transition wasn't smooth for a meaningful number of patients, a real cost alongside the real benefit.
logicChain: Brand-name use: -61%, category spending: -24%, policy goal achieved -> nurse advice line calls about access: +340% -> pharmacies report patients leaving without medication after rejection -> success in cost reduction paired with significant, separately documented access friction

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's stormwater management department compared flood incident data across neighborhoods after installing permeable pavement in select areas as part of a green infrastructure pilot. Neighborhoods with permeable pavement installed on at least 30 percent of local street surfaces reported a 44 percent reduction in minor flooding incidents during moderate rainfall events, compared to a 12 percent citywide reduction attributed to an unrelated storm drain maintenance backlog being cleared during the same period. However, during one severe rainfall event that exceeded the system's designed capacity, permeable-pavement neighborhoods and non-permeable neighborhoods showed statistically similar flooding rates, suggesting the pavement's benefit may be limited to moderate rather than severe rainfall conditions.
options: The permeable pavement showed the same flooding reduction benefit during both moderate and severe rainfall events.
The citywide reduction in flooding was entirely caused by the permeable pavement installation.
Non-permeable neighborhoods showed a larger flooding reduction than permeable-pavement neighborhoods during moderate rainfall.

The permeable pavement appears to provide a real benefit beyond general citywide improvements during moderate rainfall, but this benefit does not appear to extend to severe rainfall events that exceed the system's typical capacity.
quests.correctAnswer: The permeable pavement appears to provide a real benefit beyond general citywide improvements during moderate rainfall, but this benefit does not appear to extend to severe rainfall events that exceed the system's typical capacity.
quests.hint: Separate the moderate rainfall results, which compare permeable neighborhoods to a citywide baseline, from the specific severe rainfall event results.
quests.explanation: During moderate rainfall, permeable neighborhoods showed a substantially larger improvement (44 percent) than the general citywide trend (12 percent), suggesting a real added benefit, but this advantage disappeared during one severe event exceeding system capacity, indicating the benefit has real, specific limits under extreme conditions.
logicChain: Moderate rainfall: permeable neighborhoods -44%, citywide baseline (unrelated maintenance) -12% -> pavement shows a real added benefit beyond the baseline -> severe rainfall event exceeding capacity: permeable and non-permeable neighborhoods show similar flooding -> benefit appears real for moderate rain but limited during severe events

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A workforce development nonprofit evaluated its job training program for long-term unemployed adults across three program cohorts implemented over five years, with each cohort incorporating lessons learned from the previous one. Cohort 1, using a general skills curriculum, had a 6-month employment rate of 34 percent. Cohort 2, which added employer partnerships for guaranteed interviews upon completion, had a 6-month employment rate of 52 percent. Cohort 3, which kept the employer partnerships and added ongoing job coaching for the first 90 days of employment to help address early workplace challenges, had a 6-month employment rate of 61 percent, but also showed a notably lower rate of job loss within the first 90 days compared to Cohort 2 specifically.
options: The general skills curriculum alone in Cohort 1 accounts for the majority of the improvement seen across all three cohorts. The way the events are described throughout the passage offers no clear signal that this particular reading should be treated with any extra caution.
Cohort 3's post-placement coaching had no measurable effect on job retention compared to Cohort 2.

Each successive addition to the program, employer partnerships and then post-placement coaching, appears linked to further improvement, with the coaching specifically helping participants retain the jobs they found.
Employment rates declined with each successive cohort as changes were added.
quests.correctAnswer: Each successive addition to the program, employer partnerships and then post-placement coaching, appears linked to further improvement, with the coaching specifically helping participants retain the jobs they found.
quests.hint: Trace the employment rate increase across all three cohorts alongside the specific change added at each stage, and note the specific retention detail for Cohort 3.
quests.explanation: Employment rates rose with each addition, employer partnerships in Cohort 2 and coaching in Cohort 3, and the specific mention of lower early job loss in Cohort 3 compared to Cohort 2 supports the coaching addition as specifically linked to better job retention, not just initial placement.
logicChain: Cohort 1 (general curriculum): 34% employed at 6 months -> Cohort 2 (+ employer partnerships): 52% -> Cohort 3 (+ post-placement coaching): 61%, also lower early job loss than Cohort 2 -> each addition appears linked to further improvement, coaching specifically linked to better retention

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large hospital system's pharmacy department implemented a medication reconciliation program requiring pharmacists to review patient medication lists at both admission and discharge, aiming to reduce dangerous drug interactions. Adverse drug events fell from 4.2 to 1.8 per 1,000 patient days after implementation. The program required significant additional pharmacist staffing, and a cost-benefit analysis found the program's annual cost of $1.8 million was offset by an estimated $3.1 million in avoided costs from reduced adverse events, readmissions, and extended hospital stays. However, the analysis noted this savings estimate relied on modeling assumptions about the average cost of an adverse event that had not been independently verified against this specific hospital system's actual billing data.
options: The $3.1 million savings figure has been fully verified against the hospital's actual billing records. The passage's own account of what happened offers no particular reason to think this reading needs to be limited or qualified in any specific way.

Adverse drug events increased after the medication reconciliation program was implemented. The way the events are described throughout the passage offers no clear signal that this particular reading should be treated with any extra caution.

The program's staffing costs exceeded its estimated benefits according to the verified analysis. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.

While the program shows a clear reduction in adverse events and an estimated financial benefit, the savings figure itself rests on assumptions that have not yet been confirmed against this hospital's own actual data.
quests.correctAnswer: While the program shows a clear reduction in adverse events and an estimated financial benefit, the savings figure itself rests on assumptions that have not yet been confirmed against this hospital's own actual data.
quests.hint: Separate the clearly measured adverse event reduction from the estimated savings figure, and note the specific caveat about verification.
quests.explanation: The passage supports the adverse event reduction as a directly measured outcome, but explicitly flags the savings estimate as resting on unverified modeling assumptions rather than confirmed billing data, meaning the clinical benefit is solid while the specific financial figure carries genuine uncertainty.
logicChain: Adverse events: 4.2 to 1.8 per 1,000 patient days, directly measured -> program cost: $1.8M -> estimated savings: $3.1M, based on modeling assumptions -> savings estimate explicitly not yet verified against actual billing data -> clinical benefit solid, financial estimate carries genuine uncertainty

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A state education department studied reading proficiency after a policy change requiring third-grade students who scored below a certain threshold to receive intensive summer reading intervention before advancing to fourth grade. Students who received the intervention scored, on average, 8 points higher on the following year's reading assessment than similarly-scoring students the year before the policy began, who had not received intervention. However, the department noted that teachers, aware of the new threshold, may have engaged in more intensive in-classroom reading support throughout the regular school year for students near the threshold, a change that began the same year as the policy and was not separately measured.
options: The summer intervention program is proven to be solely responsible for the entire 8-point improvement. The passage's own account of what happened offers no particular reason to think this reading needs to be limited or qualified in any specific way.

Since increased classroom support for at-risk students may have begun alongside the summer intervention policy and wasn't measured separately, it is difficult to fully isolate how much of the improvement is due to the summer program itself.

Teachers provided less classroom support to at-risk students after the policy began. The full account given in the passage offers no particular basis for reading this any differently than as a plain, straightforward description of events.
Reading scores declined among students who received the summer intervention.
quests.correctAnswer: Since increased classroom support for at-risk students may have begun alongside the summer intervention policy and wasn't measured separately, it is difficult to fully isolate how much of the improvement is due to the summer program itself.
quests.hint: Consider what the department itself flags as a separate, unmeasured change happening at the same time as the policy.
quests.explanation: Because the department explicitly notes that classroom teaching practices for at-risk students may have shifted in the same year as the policy, without being tracked as a separate variable, this creates real ambiguity about how much of the score improvement reflects the summer program specifically versus this parallel, unmeasured classroom change.
logicChain: Students receiving summer intervention: score 8 points higher than prior-year comparable students -> teachers aware of new threshold may have increased in-classroom support the same year, unmeasured separately -> ambiguity between the summer program's effect and this parallel, untracked classroom change

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A metropolitan transit agency evaluated a fare-capping program, which automatically limits how much a rider pays in a week regardless of how many individual trips they take, aimed at making transit more affordable for frequent riders without requiring an upfront pass purchase. In the year following implementation, ridership among low-income riders, identified through a reduced-fare program enrollment, rose 28 percent, while ridership among riders not enrolled in any reduced-fare program rose 6 percent, a figure the agency attributed to general post-pandemic ridership recovery affecting all rider groups. Additionally, the agency found that riders using fare capping took an average of 1.3 more trips per week than they had the year before the program, while survey data suggested many of these additional trips were for discretionary purposes like social visits and errands rather than commuting.
options: Ridership increased at the same rate for both low-income and other riders, reflecting only the general recovery trend.
The additional trips taken by fare-capping riders were used almost entirely for commuting to work.

The program appears to have specifically benefited low-income riders beyond the general ridership recovery trend, and seems associated with riders taking on additional discretionary trips rather than only commuting more.
Fare capping led to a decrease in the number of weekly trips taken by low-income riders.
quests.correctAnswer: The program appears to have specifically benefited low-income riders beyond the general ridership recovery trend, and seems associated with riders taking on additional discretionary trips rather than only commuting more.
quests.hint: Separate the general recovery trend, seen in non-reduced-fare riders, from the larger increase specific to low-income riders, and note what the survey data says about the purpose of additional trips.
quests.explanation: Since non-reduced-fare riders' 6 percent increase is attributed to general recovery, the much larger 28 percent increase among low-income riders suggests a specific program effect beyond that baseline, and the survey data specifically points to new discretionary trips, not just commuting, as part of this expanded usage.
logicChain: Low-income riders: +28% ridership -> non-reduced-fare riders: +6%, attributed to general recovery -> fare-capping riders also average 1.3 more trips/week, mostly discretionary per survey data -> program appears to specifically benefit low-income riders and enable additional discretionary trips

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A biotechnology company's clinical trial for a new treatment showed a statistically significant improvement in the primary outcome measure compared to placebo, with 58 percent of treatment group participants showing meaningful symptom improvement versus 31 percent in the placebo group. However, the trial's secondary outcome measures, including a separately tracked measure of long-term quality of life, showed no statistically significant difference between groups, and the trial's pre-registered protocol had specified that both the primary and a designated key secondary outcome needed to show significance for the company to describe the treatment as demonstrating comprehensive clinical benefit.
options: The treatment failed to show any significant improvement on any outcome measure in the trial.
The secondary outcome measure showed a significant improvement favoring the treatment group.

The pre-registered protocol did not specify any requirements beyond the primary outcome measure. The passage's own account of what happened offers no particular reason to think this reading needs to be limited or qualified in any specific way.

While the treatment showed a real benefit on the primary measure, it did not meet the pre-specified bar the company itself had set for describing the treatment as showing comprehensive clinical benefit.
quests.correctAnswer: While the treatment showed a real benefit on the primary measure, it did not meet the pre-specified bar the company itself had set for describing the treatment as showing comprehensive clinical benefit.
quests.hint: Separate the clear success on the primary measure from the specific, pre-established bar the company set for a broader claim of benefit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large employer's diversity, equity, and inclusion initiative included mandatory bias-awareness training for all managers, restructured job posting language to reduce gendered wording, and a new structured interview rubric replacing unstructured hiring conversations. Two years after implementation, the representation of women in technical roles rose from 19 to 27 percent of new hires. A follow-up internal analysis found that job postings using the restructured language received applications from women at nearly double the rate of postings that, due to a system error, briefly reverted to old templates for about six weeks during the rollout, a natural comparison the analysis team hadn't originally planned but used opportunistically once discovered.
options: The system error proves that job posting language had no effect on who applied for these roles. Nothing about how the passage frames the surrounding circumstances would suggest this conclusion needs any further qualification or limitation.

The structured interview rubric was the only initiative found to have any measurable effect. As far as the passage's description goes, nothing about the surrounding details would suggest this needs to be treated as an incomplete picture.
Representation of women in technical roles decreased over the two-year period.

The unplanned comparison created by the brief system error offers additional, fairly direct support that the job posting language specifically affected who applied, beyond the broader combined effect of all three initiatives together.
quests.correctAnswer: The unplanned comparison created by the brief system error offers additional, fairly direct support that the job posting language specifically affected who applied, beyond the broader combined effect of all three initiatives together.
quests.hint: Consider what an unplanned, temporary reversion to old job posting language, compared against the new language, incidentally reveals.
quests.explanation: Because the six-week system error unintentionally created a natural before-and-after comparison specifically isolating job posting language from the other two initiatives, and applications from women dropped notably during that window, this offers fairly direct, if accidental, evidence for the language change's specific role, on top of the overall two-year improvement.
logicChain: Overall: women in technical hires rise from 19% to 27% over two years, three initiatives combined -> six-week system error reverts job postings to old language -> old-language postings during error: women apply at roughly half the rate of new-language postings -> accidental comparison offers fairly direct evidence for the language change's specific effect

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's public defender's office implemented a caseload cap policy limiting attorneys to no more than 120 active cases at once, down from a previous average of 190, after research suggested caseload size affected case outcomes. In the two years following implementation, the office's rate of cases resolved through favorable plea agreements or dismissals rose from 41 to 58 percent. However, the same period saw a 15 percent reduction in overall case filings citywide due to a separate policing policy change that reduced arrests for certain low-level offenses, meaning the office was handling not only fewer cases per attorney but also, city-wide, a somewhat different and possibly less complex overall mix of cases than before.
options: The caseload cap policy is proven to be solely responsible for the entire improvement in outcomes, independent of any other citywide change.
Case filings citywide increased significantly during the same two-year period.

Because case filings also dropped and the case mix may have shifted for reasons unrelated to the caseload policy, it is difficult to know how much of the improved outcome rate reflects the caseload cap itself versus this broader shift in what kinds of cases were being handled.
The policing policy change had no effect on the types of cases being filed.
quests.correctAnswer: Because case filings also dropped and the case mix may have shifted for reasons unrelated to the caseload policy, it is difficult to know how much of the improved outcome rate reflects the caseload cap itself versus this broader shift in what kinds of cases were being handled.
quests.hint: Consider how a citywide drop in low-level offense arrests might independently change the average complexity of cases attorneys are handling.
quests.explanation: Since a separate policing change reduced arrests for low-level offenses at the same time, potentially leaving a case mix that skews toward different, possibly less routine complexity than before, this confound makes it difficult to cleanly attribute the entire outcome improvement to the caseload cap alone.
logicChain: Caseload cap: 190 to 120 max cases -> outcomes improve from 41% to 58% favorable -> same period: citywide case filings drop 15% due to separate policing policy -> case mix may have shifted for unrelated reasons -> difficult to fully isolate the caseload cap's specific contribution from this broader shift

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national health insurer piloted a program offering members free access to a mental health teletherapy platform, aiming to reduce both mental health crisis-related emergency room visits and associated costs. Members who used the platform at least three times in a six-month period had a 43 percent lower rate of mental health-related emergency room visits compared to eligible members who never used the platform. However, an internal analysis found that members who chose to engage with the platform at least three times also had, on average, filled significantly more prescriptions for mental health medications in the year before the pilot began, suggesting these were members already more actively engaged in managing their mental health, independent of the new platform.
options: Since frequent platform users already showed more active mental health management before the pilot began, this pre-existing engagement likely explains part of the emergency room visit difference, not the platform alone.

The teletherapy platform is proven to be solely responsible for the entire reduction in emergency room visits. Taken together, the details the passage provides give no specific reason to treat this as anything other than a complete account of what occurred.

Members who never used the platform had filled more prescriptions than frequent platform users before the pilot began. As far as the passage's description goes, nothing about the surrounding details would suggest this needs to be treated as an incomplete picture.
Emergency room visits increased among members who used the platform frequently.
quests.correctAnswer: Since frequent platform users already showed more active mental health management before the pilot began, this pre-existing engagement likely explains part of the emergency room visit difference, not the platform alone.
quests.hint: Consider what the detail about prior-year prescription patterns reveals about who chose to engage frequently with the platform.
quests.explanation: Since members who used the platform frequently already showed higher prescription activity before the pilot even started, a sign of pre-existing active mental health management, this pre-existing engagement level likely accounts for at least part of the emergency room visit difference, complicating full credit to the platform itself.
logicChain: Frequent platform users: 43% lower ER visit rate than non-users -> frequent users also had significantly more mental health prescriptions filled BEFORE the pilot began -> pre-existing active engagement likely explains part of the difference, not the platform alone

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional airport authority evaluated the effect of a new consolidated rental car facility, which moved all rental agencies from scattered on-airport lots to a single shared facility connected by shuttle. Average time from baggage claim to driving off airport property for rental car customers dropped from 47 to 29 minutes. Customer satisfaction scores for the rental car experience specifically rose from 3.1 to 4.2 out of 5. However, satisfaction scores for the overall airport experience, which include factors like security wait times and flight delays unrelated to rental cars, showed no significant change over the same period, remaining at 3.8 out of 5 both before and after the facility opened.
options: The consolidated facility appears to have specifically improved the rental car experience without meaningfully affecting perceptions of the broader airport experience, which depends on largely unrelated factors.

Overall airport satisfaction scores rose by the same amount as rental car satisfaction scores. Every relevant detail included in the passage is consistent with treating this as a complete and accurate account, without further qualification being necessary.
Time from baggage claim to leaving the airport increased after the new facility opened.

The new facility caused a decline in customer satisfaction with the rental car experience. There is nothing in how the passage presents the sequence of events that would call for treating this conclusion as only partly supported.
quests.correctAnswer: The consolidated facility appears to have specifically improved the rental car experience without meaningfully affecting perceptions of the broader airport experience, which depends on largely unrelated factors.
quests.hint: Separate the rental-car-specific outcomes from the broader overall airport satisfaction score, and note what other factors that broader score depends on.
quests.explanation: Both time and satisfaction specific to the rental car experience improved substantially, while the passage explicitly notes the broader airport satisfaction score, dependent on unrelated factors like security and flight delays, stayed flat, showing the improvement was targeted and specific rather than reflecting a general airport-wide change.
logicChain: Rental car time: 47 to 29 min -> rental car satisfaction: 3.1 to 4.2/5 -> overall airport satisfaction (includes unrelated factors like security, delays): flat at 3.8/5 -> facility improvement appears specific to rental cars, without affecting the broader, largely unrelated overall experience

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A statewide agricultural cooperative studied the effect of a new crop insurance product designed to cover losses from increasingly erratic rainfall patterns, distinct from traditional insurance that primarily covered drought and flood as separate, discrete events. Farms enrolled in the new erratic-rainfall product reported 31 percent lower year-over-year income volatility over a five-year period compared to farms with traditional coverage. However, farms choosing the new product also, on average, diversified into a wider variety of crops during the same period, a strategy agricultural economists have independently linked to reduced income volatility regardless of insurance type, and cooperative records showed no requirement or incentive within the new insurance product specifically encouraging this diversification.
options: The new insurance product is proven to be solely responsible for the entire reduction in income volatility. The full account given in the passage offers no particular basis for reading this any differently than as a plain, straightforward description of events.

Since crop diversification is independently linked to reduced volatility and occurred among these farms without being required by the insurance product itself, it is unclear how much of the volatility reduction reflects the insurance versus this separate farming decision.
The insurance product specifically required farms to diversify their crops as a condition of coverage.
Farms with traditional coverage diversified their crops more than farms with the new product.
quests.correctAnswer: Since crop diversification is independently linked to reduced volatility and occurred among these farms without being required by the insurance product itself, it is unclear how much of the volatility reduction reflects the insurance versus this separate farming decision.
quests.hint: Consider what it means that diversification is independently linked to reduced volatility and happened without being required by the new product.
quests.explanation: Because crop diversification, a factor independently known to reduce income volatility, occurred among these farms without the insurance product requiring or incentivizing it, this creates genuine ambiguity about whether the volatility improvement reflects the insurance coverage itself, the diversification decision, or some combination of both.
logicChain: New insurance farms: -31% income volatility vs. traditional coverage farms -> new insurance farms also diversified crops more, independently linked to reduced volatility -> diversification not required or incentivized by the insurance product -> ambiguous how much of the improvement reflects insurance versus this separate farming decision

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A metropolitan school district piloted a four-day school week at five rural schools facing severe staffing shortages, with the fifth day used for optional tutoring, teacher planning, and extracurricular activities rather than being fully eliminated from student access. Teacher retention at pilot schools rose from 68 to 89 percent year-over-year, notably higher than the district's overall retention rate of 74 percent that year. Student standardized test scores at pilot schools showed no statistically significant change compared to the two years prior. However, the district noted that pilot schools were specifically selected because they had the most severe staffing shortages and lowest retention to begin with, meaning some improvement toward the district average might have been expected regardless of the schedule change, a statistical pattern sometimes called reversion to the mean.
options: Standardized test scores improved significantly at the pilot schools after the schedule change. Nothing about how the passage frames the surrounding circumstances would suggest this conclusion needs any further qualification or limitation.

Pilot schools were selected because they already had the district's highest retention rates. The passage's own account of what happened offers no particular reason to think this reading needs to be limited or qualified in any specific way.

While retention improved substantially at pilot schools, the fact that they started from an unusually low baseline means some of that improvement might have occurred even without the schedule change, complicating how much credit the four-day week itself deserves.
Teacher retention decreased at the pilot schools after adopting the four-day week.
quests.correctAnswer: While retention improved substantially at pilot schools, the fact that they started from an unusually low baseline means some of that improvement might have occurred even without the schedule change, complicating how much credit the four-day week itself deserves.
quests.hint: Consider what the district's own note about 'reversion to the mean' suggests about interpreting a jump from an unusually low starting point.
quests.explanation: Since pilot schools were specifically chosen for having the district's worst retention, some natural improvement toward the district average might occur regardless of any intervention, a statistical pattern the district itself flags, meaning the four-day week's specific contribution to the retention jump is harder to confidently isolate.
logicChain: Pilot schools selected specifically for worst staffing/retention -> retention rises from 68% to 89%, above district average of 74% -> district notes this could partly reflect natural reversion toward the mean from an unusually low starting point -> schedule change's specific contribution to the improvement is harder to confidently isolate

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national fitness equipment manufacturer studied customer outcomes after introducing an AI-powered form-correction feature in its connected home gym equipment, which used camera-based tracking to give real-time feedback on exercise technique. Among users who enabled the feature and received at least one correction per week, reported injury rates over one year were 2.1 percent, compared to 6.8 percent among users who had access to the feature but chose not to enable it. However, users who enabled the feature also completed, on average, 40 percent more workouts per month than non-enabling users, and exercise frequency itself is independently associated with better movement patterns and lower injury risk as users become more practiced and consistent over time.
options: Since feature-enabling users also exercised substantially more often, a factor independently linked to lower injury risk, it is difficult to fully separate the form-correction feature's specific effect from the effect of simply exercising more consistently.

The form-correction feature is proven to be solely responsible for the entire difference in injury rates. Nothing about how the passage frames the surrounding circumstances would suggest this conclusion needs any further qualification or limitation.
Users who enabled the feature completed fewer workouts per month than users who did not.

Exercise frequency has no independent relationship to injury risk according to established research. Reading through everything the passage lays out, there is no specific detail that would push against treating this as the straightforward explanation.
quests.correctAnswer: Since feature-enabling users also exercised substantially more often, a factor independently linked to lower injury risk, it is difficult to fully separate the form-correction feature's specific effect from the effect of simply exercising more consistently.
quests.hint: Consider what the independent link between exercise frequency and injury risk means for interpreting the injury rate difference between these two groups.
quests.explanation: Because feature-enabling users also worked out significantly more often, and increased consistency is independently linked to lower injury risk regardless of any specific feedback tool, this overlapping factor makes it difficult to confidently attribute the full injury rate difference to the form-correction feature alone.
logicChain: Feature-enabled users: 2.1% injury rate, also 40% more monthly workouts -> non-enabled users: 6.8% injury rate, fewer workouts -> exercise frequency independently linked to lower injury risk -> difficult to fully separate the feature's specific effect from the effect of exercising more consistently

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A multinational logistics company evaluated a predictive maintenance system for its delivery truck fleet, which used sensor data to flag vehicles likely to need repair before a breakdown occurred. Trucks using the system had 52 percent fewer unplanned breakdowns over eighteen months compared to trucks using traditional scheduled maintenance alone. The system was rolled out fleet-wide simultaneously, with no control group of similar trucks continuing traditional maintenance during the same period; the 52 percent figure instead compares this fleet's breakdown rate after the rollout to the same fleet's own breakdown rate during the eighteen months prior. During the comparison period before rollout, the company had also renegotiated its parts supplier contract, resulting in access to higher-quality replacement components used in all repairs, both routine and predictive, from that point forward.
options: The predictive maintenance system is proven to be solely responsible for the entire breakdown reduction, independent of the parts contract change. Nothing in the way the passage lays out these events gives any real reason to treat this as an incomplete or qualified reading of what took place.
The comparison included a separate control group of similar trucks using only traditional maintenance during the same eighteen months.

Since there was no separate comparison group and a parts quality change happened at roughly the same time as the system's rollout, it is difficult to confidently isolate how much of the breakdown reduction is due to the predictive system itself versus the improved parts.
The parts supplier contract change occurred well after the predictive system had already been evaluated.
quests.correctAnswer: Since there was no separate comparison group and a parts quality change happened at roughly the same time as the system's rollout, it is difficult to confidently isolate how much of the breakdown reduction is due to the predictive system itself versus the improved parts.
quests.hint: Notice both that there is no true control group and that a second, unrelated change happened around the same time as the system rollout.
quests.explanation: Without a contemporaneous control group, the comparison relies entirely on before-and-after data from the same fleet, and since a parts quality improvement also happened around the same time, affecting all repairs, this creates a genuine confound that makes isolating the predictive system's specific contribution difficult.
logicChain: Predictive system rolled out fleet-wide, no control group -> compares fleet's own before/after breakdown rates -> parts supplier contract also renegotiated around the same time, improving quality of all repairs -> lack of control group plus simultaneous parts change makes it difficult to isolate the system's specific contribution

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national nonprofit evaluated a financial literacy program delivered through employer partnerships, where companies offered the program as a voluntary benefit to employees. Employees who completed the program showed a 24 percent increase in retirement savings contribution rates within one year, compared to no significant change among eligible employees who did not complete the program. A deeper analysis found that employees at companies offering an employer match on retirement contributions were far more likely to both enroll in the financial literacy program and increase their savings rate, while employees at companies without a match rarely completed the program and showed little change in savings behavior regardless of program availability, suggesting the presence of a match may be a necessary condition for the program's apparent effect.
options: The program's effectiveness appears closely tied to whether an employer match is available, suggesting the financial literacy training alone, without a matching incentive, may have limited impact.
The financial literacy program was equally effective at increasing savings rates regardless of whether an employer match existed.
Employees at companies without an employer match were more likely to complete the program than those with a match.
Retirement savings contribution rates decreased among employees who completed the program.
quests.correctAnswer: The program's effectiveness appears closely tied to whether an employer match is available, suggesting the financial literacy training alone, without a matching incentive, may have limited impact.
quests.hint: Notice the specific finding that separates program completion and effectiveness by whether a matching incentive existed.
quests.explanation: The deeper analysis reveals the program's apparent success is concentrated specifically among employees with access to a matching incentive, while it had little completion or effect at companies without one, suggesting the match itself may be a necessary condition rather than the training being independently effective on its own.
logicChain: Overall: program completers show +24% savings rate vs. non-completers, no change -> deeper analysis: match-offering companies show high completion and savings increase -> no-match companies: rare completion, little change -> program effectiveness appears closely tied to match availability, suggesting limited standalone impact

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional water utility studied the effect of a tiered pricing structure that charged progressively higher rates for water use above certain monthly thresholds, aiming to reduce peak-season residential water consumption. Average household water use during the summer months dropped 19 percent in the first year after implementation. However, that same summer also brought 30 percent more rainfall than the historical average, which independently reduces outdoor irrigation needs, a fact the utility's own hydrologist flagged as a significant confound. In the second year, when rainfall returned to a near-normal level, water use remained 11 percent below the pre-pricing baseline, still a meaningful reduction but notably smaller than the first year's drop.
options: The entire reduction in water use across both years is fully explained by rainfall, with the pricing structure having no independent effect.
Water use in the second year returned completely to the pre-pricing baseline with no lasting reduction.

The pricing structure appears to have a real, lasting effect on water use, though the first year's larger reduction was likely inflated by unusually high rainfall that reduced irrigation needs independent of the pricing policy.
Rainfall in the first year was below the historical average, increasing the need for irrigation.
quests.correctAnswer: The pricing structure appears to have a real, lasting effect on water use, though the first year's larger reduction was likely inflated by unusually high rainfall that reduced irrigation needs independent of the pricing policy.
quests.hint: Compare the first year's larger reduction, which coincided with unusually high rainfall, to the second year's smaller but still meaningful reduction under more typical rainfall.
quests.explanation: The first year's especially large reduction is complicated by unusually high rainfall reducing irrigation needs regardless of pricing, a confound the utility itself acknowledges, but the second year's continued, smaller reduction under near-normal rainfall suggests the pricing structure does have a genuine, lasting effect beyond what rainfall alone would explain.
logicChain: Year 1: water use -19%, but rainfall 30% above average (independent confound) -> Year 2: rainfall near normal, water use still -11% vs. pre-pricing baseline -> continued reduction under typical rainfall suggests a real, lasting pricing effect, though smaller than the rainfall-inflated first-year figure

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large multi-site healthcare system implemented an AI-assisted diagnostic imaging review tool intended to flag potential abnormalities on radiology scans for radiologist review, aiming to reduce missed diagnoses without significantly slowing down radiologist workflow. Across twelve participating hospitals, the rate of diagnoses missed on initial review and later identified as errors dropped from 3.4 to 1.9 per 1,000 scans in the year following implementation. However, results varied considerably by hospital: the four hospitals with the highest baseline radiologist caseloads per shift, already operating under significant time pressure before the tool's introduction, showed the largest error reductions, from an average of 4.8 to 1.7 per 1,000 scans. The four hospitals with the lowest baseline caseloads showed a smaller reduction, from 2.1 to 1.6 per 1,000 scans. Additionally, average time per scan review increased by 90 seconds system-wide, a change hospital administrators noted was smaller than initially feared but still represented a real trade-off in radiologist throughput.
options: The tool provided the largest benefit at hospitals with the lowest baseline caseloads and least time pressure. Nothing in the way the passage lays out these events gives any real reason to treat this as an incomplete or qualified reading of what took place.

The tool appears to provide a meaningfully larger error-reduction benefit at hospitals where radiologists were already under the greatest time pressure, while requiring a modest but real increase in review time across all hospitals.
Average review time per scan decreased after the tool was implemented.
Error rates increased at every hospital after the tool was introduced, regardless of baseline caseload.
quests.correctAnswer: The tool appears to provide a meaningfully larger error-reduction benefit at hospitals where radiologists were already under the greatest time pressure, while requiring a modest but real increase in review time across all hospitals.
quests.hint: Compare the size of the error reduction between the high-caseload and low-caseload hospital groups, and separately note the review time trade-off that applies across the whole system.
quests.explanation: The high-caseload hospitals, likely benefiting most from an assistive tool when radiologists are already stretched thin, showed a much larger error reduction (4.8 to 1.7) than the lower-caseload hospitals (2.1 to 1.6), while the system-wide 90-second increase in review time represents a separate, genuine trade-off acknowledged even by hospital administrators, showing a nuanced overall picture of uneven benefit alongside a real cost.
logicChain: System-wide error rate: 3.4 to 1.9 per 1,000 scans -> high-caseload hospitals: 4.8 to 1.7 (larger reduction) -> low-caseload hospitals: 2.1 to 1.6 (smaller reduction) -> review time: +90 seconds system-wide, a real but smaller-than-feared trade-off -> tool shows uneven, larger benefit where time pressure was greatest, alongside a modest but genuine cost

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national retail bank evaluated an algorithmic credit-decisioning system intended to expand access to credit for applicants with limited traditional credit history by incorporating alternative data such as rent and utility payment consistency. Approval rates for applicants with thin credit files rose from 22 to 41 percent after implementation, and the default rate among these newly approved applicants was 6.8 percent, compared to a default rate of 7.1 percent among applicants with traditional credit files approved through the conventional process, suggesting the alternative data was identifying creditworthy applicants effectively. However, a fair-lending audit found that approval rate increases were substantially smaller for applicants in zip codes with historically lower rates of formal rental and utility record-keeping, often overlapping with lower-income areas, since the alternative data the algorithm relied on was less consistently available for applicants from those areas.
options: The algorithm increased default rates significantly compared to the conventional credit-decisioning process.

While the algorithm appears effective overall at identifying creditworthy applicants using alternative data, its benefit was not evenly distributed, applicants in areas with less consistent formal record-keeping saw smaller gains in approval access.
Approval rate increases were largest specifically in areas with less consistent formal rental and utility record-keeping.
The fair-lending audit found no meaningful difference in outcomes across different geographic areas.
quests.correctAnswer: While the algorithm appears effective overall at identifying creditworthy applicants using alternative data, its benefit was not evenly distributed, applicants in areas with less consistent formal record-keeping saw smaller gains in approval access.
quests.hint: Separate the overall positive findings, approval rate and default rate, from the specific, uneven pattern the fair-lending audit uncovered across different areas.
quests.explanation: The passage supports a genuinely two-part conclusion: the algorithm succeeded at its core goal, expanding access with a comparable or even slightly better default rate, but the audit's specific finding about uneven benefit tied to record-keeping consistency shows the improvement wasn't distributed equally across all applicant populations, a real limitation alongside the real success.
logicChain: Thin-file approval rate: 22% to 41% -> new approvals' default rate: 6.8%, comparable to traditional approvals' 7.1% -> algorithm appears effective overall -> fair-lending audit: smaller approval gains in areas with less consistent formal record-keeping, often lower-income -> overall success paired with an uneven, documented distributional limitation

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A state department of corrections evaluated a cognitive-behavioral therapy program for incarcerated individuals nearing release, aiming to reduce recidivism, tracking outcomes over three years for two program cohorts implemented a year apart with refinements made between them based on the first cohort's results. Cohort 1 participants had a two-year recidivism rate of 34 percent, compared to 41 percent among a matched comparison group of eligible non-participants, a modest but statistically significant difference. Program staff, noting that Cohort 1 participants with fewer than eight completed sessions showed almost no improvement over the comparison group, while those completing twelve or more sessions showed recidivism rates below 25 percent, redesigned Cohort 2 to require a minimum of twelve sessions for program credit rather than allowing partial completion to count. Cohort 2, entirely composed of participants who completed twelve or more sessions under this new requirement, showed a recidivism rate of 23 percent against a comparison group rate of 40 percent, a larger gap than Cohort 1's overall result.
options: Cohort 1 participants who completed fewer than eight sessions showed the strongest reduction in recidivism.

Cohort 2's redesign removed the minimum session requirement entirely, allowing any level of completion to count. Every relevant detail included in the passage is consistent with treating this as a complete and accurate account, without further qualification being necessary.

The program's benefit appears concentrated among participants completing a higher number of sessions, and requiring this threshold for Cohort 2 produced a larger, more consistent effect than Cohort 1's mixed-completion results.
The comparison group's recidivism rate was lower than the participants' rate in both cohorts.
quests.correctAnswer: The program's benefit appears concentrated among participants completing a higher number of sessions, and requiring this threshold for Cohort 2 produced a larger, more consistent effect than Cohort 1's mixed-completion results.
quests.hint: Trace the specific finding about session completion within Cohort 1, how it informed Cohort 2's redesign, and compare the two cohorts' overall results.
quests.explanation: Cohort 1's internal breakdown revealed the benefit was concentrated among higher-session completers, informing Cohort 2's redesign requiring exactly that threshold, and Cohort 2's subsequent larger, more consistent gap compared to its own comparison group supports the session-completion threshold as key to a stronger, more reliable program effect.
logicChain: Cohort 1: <8 sessions shows almost no improvement, 12+ sessions shows <25% recidivism vs ~41% comparison -> Cohort 2 redesigned to require 12+ sessions for credit -> Cohort 2: 23% recidivism vs 40% comparison, a larger, more consistent gap than Cohort 1's overall mixed result -> session completion threshold appears key to a stronger, more reliable effect
